title: Generative design of de novo AAV vectors with unique serological profiles
summary: More than 5000 monogenic diseases are potentially curable by replacing a single defective gene with one that functions normally. Currently, the only clinically approved vector able to effectively deliver a therapeutic gene to a target tissue is Adeno-Associated Viruses (AAVs). However, despite decades of work, only a handful of gene replacement therapies have been approved, and many patients remain ineligible for even those. A major barrier to broad adoption of AAV therapies is pre-existing immunity to AAVs, mediated by neutralizing antibodies (nAbs). It is potentially possible to change exposed capsid surfaces in AAV capsids to avoid nAb recognition. However, traditional techniques such as rational design and directed evolution only allow modest changes. AAV function becomes compromised long before full nAb avoidance is achieved. Recent advances in protein design by generative modelling provide a new way to overcome this problem by learning AAV design constraints from natural sequences. We built a variational autoencoder that could learn these sequence constraints and generate functional AAV capsid proteins de novo. More than 255 designs were synthesized and tested in vitro in two design sets, with one set dedicated to exploring uncertain regions of the sequence space. Between the two campaigns, seven designs transduced human cells with >50% efficiency, of which four avoided nAb neutralization (NT50 < 1:50) in all human sera that were reactive to AAV. In one of these designs, sequence identity to the nearest natural AAV sequence was 18% divergent. Given the radical sequence diversity and its unique serological profile, this new capsid design would represent the first ever AAV serotype designed de novo.

AI.tldr: 생성형 인공지능(VAE)을 활용하여 기존 환자의 중화항체를 완벽히 회피하면서도 인간 세포 전달 효율을 유지하는 새로운 de novo AAV 캡시드 혈청형을 개발했습니다.
AI.motivation: AAV(아데노부속바이러스)는 유전자 치료제의 핵심 전달체이나, 환자 체내에 이미 존재하는 중화항체(nAb)로 인한 면역 반응이 치료제 적용의 심각한 걸림돌이 되고 있습니다. 기존의 합리적 설계나 지향성 진화 기법은 서열 변형 가능 범위가 제한적이어서, 완전한 중화항체 회피가 이루어지기 전에 캡시드의 기능이 저하되는 한계가 있었습니다.
AI.method: 자연계 AAV 서열의 설계 제약 조건을 학습하여 기능적인 AAV 캡시드 단백질을 de novo 생성할 수 있는 변이형 오토인코더(Variational Autoencoder, VAE) 모델을 구축했습니다. 이를 통해 서열 공간의 미개척 영역을 탐색하는 세트를 포함하여 두 차례의 설계 캠페인을 거쳐 총 255개 이상의 변이체를 합성하고 in vitro 실험을 통해 기능성을 검증했습니다.
AI.result: 합성된 변이체 중 7개 디자인이 인간 세포에서 50% 이상의 유전자 전달(형질도입) 효율을 나타냈으며, 이 중 4개는 AAV 반응성 인간 혈청 전체에 대해 중화항체 중화 반응을 완벽히 회피(NT50 < 1:50)했습니다. 특히 한 디자인은 가장 가까운 자연계 AAV 서열과 18%나 다른 서열 다양성을 확보했습니다.
AI.conclusion: 본 연구는 생성형 AI를 통해 기존 자연계 서열과 상당한 차이를 가지면서도 기능성과 면역 회피능을 동시에 갖춘 사상 최초의 de novo AAV 혈청형을 설계하는 데 성공했습니다. 이는 기존 면역 반응으로 인해 유전자 치료를 받지 못했던 환자들에게 새로운 치료 기회를 제공할 수 있는 획기적인 성과입니다.

title: Towards a best-in-class IgE disruptor for food allergy with Claude-enabled antibody design
summary: Food allergy affects an estimated 220–250 million people worldwide, for whom the constant risk of a severe reaction weighs heavily on quality of life. Allergic reactions are triggered by the cross-linking of allergen-specific IgE bound to its high-affinity receptor, FcϵRI, on mast cells and basophils, causing degranulation, inflammation and, in severe cases, anaphylaxis. Omalizumab (Xolair), the sole FDA-approved biologic for food allergy, neutralizes circulating IgE; however, it does not effectively remove IgE from FcϵRI, where it can persist for weeks and where even a small residual amount can sustain sensitivity. Here we describe an agentic computational design campaign with Claude toward a disruptive inhibitor antibody that physically removes bound IgE from FcϵRI. Guided by our research team, Claude pursued a biparatopic molecule that pairs a disruptor arm, which displaces IgE from FcϵRI, with a non-competing anchor arm that holds the molecule on receptor-bound IgE. Of 91 experimentally characterized disruptor designs, 20 showed activity against receptor-bound IgE by competitive bio-layer interferometry, and in a dose-titration assay three variants removed more IgE than omalizumab at therapeutically relevant concentrations (25–400 nM). De novo designs for the anchor arm bound IgE at diverse epitopes with apparent affinities of 3.4–235 nM. These subcomponents provide the starting point for further characterization toward a best-in-class IgE disruptor.
